name: Romeo
description: The only son of Montague, a passionate young man who pines for Rosaline until he meets Juliet at the Capulet feast and falls instantly, wholly in love. He marries her in secret, is banished for killing Tybalt, and kills himself at her tomb believing her dead.

name: Juliet
description: Capulet's only daughter, not yet fourteen, who grows from an obedient child into a resolute young woman in the space of a few days. She secretly marries Romeo, defies her father's plan to wed Paris, takes a sleeping potion to escape it, and stabs herself when she wakes to find Romeo dead.

name: Mercutio
description: A kinsman of Prince Escalus and Romeo's quick-witted, mercurial friend, famous for the fanciful Queen Mab speech and a torrent of bawdy puns. Neither Montague nor Capulet, he is drawn into the feud and slain by Tybalt under Romeo's arm, cursing 'a plague o' both your houses.'

name: Benvolio
description: Montague's nephew and Romeo's level-headed cousin, a peacemaker who tries to stop the opening brawl and to coax Romeo out of his lovesickness. He reports the deaths in the street fight truthfully to the Prince, then disappears from the play.

name: Tybalt
description: Lady Capulet's nephew, a hot-tempered swordsman who treats the feud as a point of honour. He spots Romeo at the feast and burns to fight him; the next day he kills Mercutio and is killed by Romeo, the act that gets Romeo banished and sets the tragedy in motion.

name: Nurse
description: Juliet's wet-nurse and lifelong companion, earthy, talkative, and bawdy. She acts as go-between for the lovers and helps arrange the secret marriage, but loses Juliet's trust when she advises her to forget the banished Romeo and marry Paris instead.

name: Friar Lawrence
description: A Franciscan friar and herbalist who is Romeo's confessor. Hoping to reconcile the two houses, he secretly marries Romeo and Juliet and devises the sleeping-potion plan; when his letter to Romeo miscarries, the scheme ends in both lovers' deaths.

relationships.relation: fellow friar, entrusts the letter to

name: Capulet
description: The head of the house of Capulet and Juliet's father. Genial host at the feast, he at first counsels patience over the marriage, but turns tyrannical when Juliet refuses Paris, threatening to disown her. He is reconciled with Montague over their children's bodies.

name: Lady Capulet
description: Juliet's mother, cooler and more distant than the Nurse, who urges the match with Paris and, after Tybalt's death, demands Romeo's life. She is unable to soften her husband when he turns on their daughter.

name: Paris
description: A young count and kinsman of the Prince who seeks Juliet's hand with Capulet's blessing. Courteous and sincere, he mourns at her tomb, where he fights and is killed by Romeo, asking with his last breath to be laid beside her.

name: Prince Escalus
description: The Prince of Verona, who tries to keep civil peace between the warring houses. He decrees death for further brawling, banishes Romeo rather than executing him, and pronounces the play's closing judgment that 'all are punish'd.'

name: Montague
description: The head of the house of Montague and Romeo's father, worried over his son's secret melancholy early in the play. He reports that grief over Romeo's banishment has killed his wife, and vows to raise a golden statue of Juliet in reconciliation.

name: Lady Montague
description: Romeo's mother, who appears only briefly to stay her husband from the opening brawl and to ask after her son. Montague later reports that she has died of grief at Romeo's exile.

name: Sampson
description: A swaggering servant of the Capulets who, with Gregory, starts the street brawl that opens the play by biting his thumb at the Montague men. His talk is full of bluster and bawdy jokes about Montague maids.

name: Gregory
description: A servant of the Capulets who trades quibbles with Sampson and helps provoke the opening fight with the house of Montague.

name: Abraham
description: A servant of the Montagues who confronts Sampson and Gregory in the opening scene, demanding whether they bite their thumb at him.

name: Balthasar
description: Romeo's faithful servant, who brings him the false news in Mantua that Juliet is dead and lies buried in the Capulet vault, then accompanies him to the tomb.

name: Peter
description: A comic servant attending the Nurse, who carries her fan, fails to defend her from Mercutio's mockery, and banters with the musicians after Juliet is found apparently dead.

name: Second Capulet
description: An elderly kinsman of Capulet (the 'cousin Capulet' and old uncle of the cast list) who sits with him at the feast reminiscing about how many years it has been since they last wore a masker's costume.

name: Friar John
description: A Franciscan of the same order as Friar Lawrence, sent to carry the crucial letter to Romeo in Mantua. Quarantined in a plague-sealed house, he never delivers it, and the failure dooms the lovers' plan.

name: Apothecary
description: A poor, gaunt druggist of Mantua who, against the law and his own conscience, sells Romeo the deadly poison because his poverty leaves him no choice.

name: Chorus
description: A single speaker who delivers the two sonnet-form prologues, to Act 1 ('Two households, both alike in dignity...') and Act 2, framing the action and announcing the 'pair of star-cross'd lovers' before the story begins.

name: Page
description: Count Paris's young page, who keeps watch at the churchyard, whistles a warning when Romeo approaches, and runs to fetch the watch after the fatal fight at the tomb.

name: First Citizen
description: An officer of the watch and citizen of Verona who rouses the townsfolk against the brawling households with the cry 'Clubs, bills, and partisans!' and later helps secure the scene of the killings.

name: First Musician
description: One of the musicians hired for Juliet's wedding, left idle when the celebration becomes a funeral; he trades jokes with Peter about a doleful tune and a dinner.

name: Second Musician
description: A wedding musician who banters with Peter and the other players after Juliet is discovered as if dead.

name: Third Musician
description: The third of the wedding musicians dismissed when Juliet's marriage feast is turned to mourning.

name: Servant
description: Various unnamed serving-men of the Capulet household. One, unable to read, asks Romeo to decipher the guest list and so unwittingly invites him to the feast; others prepare the hall and run errands.

name: First Servant
description: A Capulet serving-man clearing the great hall after the feast, calling for help to take away the plate and stools.

name: Second Servant
description: A second Capulet serving-man, busy with the bustle of the household before the feast and the aborted wedding.

name: First Watchman
description: The chief watchman who discovers the bodies at the Capulet tomb, takes Balthasar and Friar Lawrence into custody, and summons the Prince.

name: Second Watchman
description: A watchman who helps secure the churchyard after the deaths at the tomb.

name: Third Watchman
description: A watchman who helps guard the churchyard and the captured friar in the play's final scene.
